# EDGE Screener: design under the lens "simplicity and ownership first"

Evidence base: the brief and follow-up, the ten audit reports, the four adversarial verifications (they override the audits where they refute them), the repository at HEAD `641e55e` (audits ran at `3db84ae`; the only later commit adds ERRORS D22/D23, `git log 3db84ae..HEAD`), and four bounded read-only queries of mine (2026-10-27, cited as "my query"). Labels: **FACT** (cited), **INFERENCE**, **PROPOSED**, **UNKNOWN**.

## 0. The design in one paragraph, and why it is the simplest one that is correct

**PROPOSED.** One new private Node 22 service, `screener-worker`, owns all screening computation. It keeps **one in-memory, full-history snapshot of the market per data version**. It reads that snapshot **once per version** from PostgreSQL through a new read-only login. It evaluates every technical value with the one shared formula module `apps/edge-bff/terminal/src/calc/indicators.ts` `F`, through the existing pure core (`registry.ts`, `conditions.ts`, `flow.ts`, `datafile.ts`, `signals.ts`), imported read-only and never copied.

The parts around it:
- **The "precomputed default layer"** is that snapshot's memo for each data version. It is not a table.
- **Feature 04** is unchanged. It becomes the screener's parity oracle in tests and stays the AI's source.
- **edge-bff** gains a relay module (`app/screener.py`) and a thin Vite sub-app (`apps/edge-bff/screener/`). The sub-app renders only and contains no formula code.
- **Flow** reads one bounded Feature 05 window per broker version through `flow.ts`, plus the stored Feature 06 columns that need long history.
- **Saved screens** start in the browser (Phase 1) and move to `edge_bff` tables (Phase 3).
- **Send to Backtest** is a page-only import in the Backtest page. The backtest worker is untouched.

| Component | This design | Publisher-file alternative | Extend-Feature-04 alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| New services | 1 (`screener-worker`) | 1 | 1 (still need dynamic compute) |
| Changed CLI-deployed services | 0 | 2 (terminal-publisher, terminal-api) | 1 (stockbit-updater engine copy) + 3 scripts |
| Feature 04 change | none | none | VERSION bump, ~45 dual implementations, full rewrite, checkpoint re-bootstrap |
| DB schema change in Phase 1 | 1 role/grant migration (no table) | none, but flow still needs DB | migrations on 2 tables + catalogs |
| backtest-worker change | none | none | none |
| Formula implementations | 1 (`F`) | 1 + Python ranking for flow files | 2 more per indicator (TA-Lib + streaming) |

**INFERENCE from the table:** this design changes the fewest deployed components (FACT inputs: feature04.md §11, verify_feature04 F04-14, reuse.md §3.4, flow.md §5).

---

## T1. Where screening computation runs

**Need.** Evaluate up to 844 stocks at once against default and custom parameters of the 53 registry indicators, plus flow and price-action conditions. Return values per condition, at interactive latency, without risking the Backtest.

**Evidence.**
- **FACT:** `F` is the single formula module shared by the Terminal chart, the Backtest page and the backtest worker (reuse.md §0.1). The pure core runs under Node unchanged (benchmark.md §0).
- **FACT, compute cost on one thread, full history, all 845 tickers (benchmark.md §2a-2d):**
  - RSI(7) + `rsi<30`: 80–124 ms.
  - SMA(75) state: 90–141 ms.
  - MACD cross within 5 bars: 162–251 ms.
  - All three on one `Calc`: 354–564 ms.
  - All 53 defaults: 8.1–10.2 s.
- **FACT, the backtest worker:**
  - It has exactly two compute threads, one preview at a time and a 12-stock cap (`engine.ts:151`, reuse.md §3.2).
  - Its memory was sized for 12 stocks (1.31 GB peak, README).
  - It has **no Postgres or bucket credentials by design**, "so the worker reads the bars the Terminal draws" (`apps/backtest-worker/src/terminal.ts:1-3`, `apps/edge-bff/backtest/CONTRACT.md` §1).
  - Its `engine_version` hashes every `*.ts`/`*.json` in `apps/edge-bff/backtest/src/core` and every `*.ts` in `apps/backtest-worker/src` (`apps/backtest-worker/src/version.ts:16-31`).
- **FACT:** edge-bff's runtime role can read 0 of 87 public relations (edge_conventions.md §1.3). edge-bff is Python.

**Options and verdicts.**
- **Browser (rejected).** A cold full-market screen needs 845 `/bundle` grants and 845 downloads: an estimated 50 s to 2.5 min, refused under the default quotas of 30 tickers per hour. The user's device does the work (benchmark.md §4, INFERENCE from FACT inputs).
- **Thread or route in backtest-worker (rejected).**
  - It shares the process and memory the Backtest depends on.
  - A full-market data path needs either DB credentials, which contradicts the worker's stated design, or publisher and terminal-api changes.
  - Any screener file under `apps/backtest-worker/src` or `backtest/src/core` changes the Backtest's `engine_version` label (FACT, version.ts).
  - The user requires that the worker must not break.
- **SQL in PostgreSQL (rejected).** It would re-implement the 53 formulas, which the brief's hard constraint forbids. Feature 04 stores only 9 of them (verify_feature04 F04-17).
- **edge-bff in Python (rejected).** That would be a second formula implementation.
- **New private `screener-worker` (CHOSEN, PROPOSED).** Node 22 with type stripping, the backtest worker's module loader (`loader/register.mjs`, copied into the image as-is) and the house private-service pattern: key header, deadline, caller watch, JSON logs (reuse.md §1.2-1.3).

**Ownership (PROPOSED).**

| Owner | Owns |
|---|---|
| `screener-worker` | snapshot, versions, condition evaluation, planner, screener sidecar contract, presets, flow window, catalog |
| edge-bff | session, CSRF and Origin, relay, the page, the shell tab, saved screens (Phase 3) |
| shared core and `indicators.ts` | formulas, parameter validation, comparison rules, flow sums (no change) |
| Backtest page | interpreting an imported screen (Phase 3) |

**Contention.**
- **INFERENCE:** there is no contention with Backtest jobs or previews, because it is a separate process.
- **INFERENCE:** the database sees one full price read per data version, about 2–3 a day plus restarts (T2).

**Deploy (PROPOSED).**
- GitHub `main`, `rootDirectory "/"`, `dockerfilePath apps/screener-worker/Dockerfile`, with `watchPatterns` on `/apps/screener-worker/**`, `/apps/edge-bff/backtest/src/core/**`, `/apps/edge-bff/terminal/src/calc/**` and `/apps/edge-bff/terminal/src/data/indRegistry.json`.
- Precedent: `feature-04-worker` (FACT, `.railway/railway.ts:162-169`).
- **Rejected: CLI upload**, as backtest-worker uses. Page and server would then be released separately. With GitHub, a shared-core change redeploys both together. M252 (merge commit skipped) still applies: check the deployment for each merge commit.

**Credentials (PROPOSED).**
- The read-only DB login lives only in `screener-worker`.
- The worker key is shared with edge-bff by Railway reference, as `BACKTEST_WORKER_KEY` is.

**Class of problem (INFERENCE).** This is a cross-sectional computation over data that is published per entity. Planned cross-asset and macro screens hit the same mechanism. In this design they become another snapshot source with a read grant, not another service.

**Covers:** every screener computation. **Does not cover:** the AI's access to screener results (a later onboarding).

**Cost and risk:**
- One more service to run.
- One npm dependency: a Postgres client, pinned exactly with a lockfile. The backtest worker has none (FACT, its Dockerfile header).

**Verification:**
- backtest-worker tests and `registry:check` stay green.
- The worker's `engine_version` is unchanged after the screener lands (a test that recomputes it).
- **Permanent.**

---

## T2. Market-data path, data version and as-of policy

**Need.** Custom parameters need full history (FACT, measured):
- With only the last 1,000 bars, EMA 200 differs on 508 of 575 tickers (verify_matrix_a a-precompute).
- KAMA on BABP is still 1.3e-3 off after 1,000 bars.
- Cumulative levels never converge (matrix_b §3).

The brief forbids querying large raw tables per request.

**Options.**
- **Per-request Postgres reads (rejected).** Multi-day Feature 04 windows take 2.2–2.6 s cold, and a 3-year price window has taken up to 16 s on its first touch (benchmark.md §3).
- **Per-ticker packs through terminal-api (rejected).** See T1: per-ticker grants, quotas, minutes.
- **A published cross-sectional file (rejected for now).** It changes two CLI-deployed services and depends on the open M250 fix (content-addressed keys). The rack has no cross-sectional flow product either, so the screener would need a DB path anyway (flow.md §6).
- **In-memory snapshot, loaded once per data version from PostgreSQL through a read-only role (CHOSEN, PROPOSED).**

**Load (PROPOSED).**
- One streamed statement: `SELECT ticker, date, open, high, low, close, volume FROM "Price_Stock_Indonesia_IDX" WHERE timeframe='Daily' AND is_final ORDER BY ticker, date`.
  - **FACT:** server time 1.37–3.0 s for 1,330,722 rows (benchmark.md §3).
  - **UNKNOWN:** transfer time inside Railway, to be measured in Phase 17.
- Each ticker's rows are wrapped as a columnar `price-pack` document and passed to `priceSeries` (`datafile.ts:139-163`). The bar-building rule is therefore the Terminal's and the Backtest's by construction: a row without four finite prices is dropped, and a null volume stays null.
- **FACT:** memory is 229 MB RSS after load and 279 MB peak, measured with JSON input (benchmark.md §2).
- **FACT:** `F` on that DB history equals stored Feature 04 for 15 columns on all 828 equity rows of 2026-10-27, max relative difference 1.16e-15 (benchmark.md §2f).

**Data version (PROPOSED).**
- `price_version` is the first 16 hex characters of the sha256 over the canonical row stream. It is content-addressed, the same mechanism as the worker's `engineVersion`, so it is never a hand-kept number. A reload with unchanged data gives the same version and keeps the memo.
- **Reload trigger.**
  - A probe every 60 s of `max(id)` in `Monitoring_Price_ALL`. **FACT:** the price cron writes one row per run, for example ids 126 and 127 for 2026-10-27, finished 10:04:51 UTC; RECOVERY runs write rows around 23:04 UTC (my query).
  - A safety reload every 6 h for history rewrites outside the cron (the planned 09-17/18 refill, a future D22 fix). **UNKNOWN:** whether those write a monitoring row.
- **Not used as signals:**
  - publisher `state.json` (not on this path);
  - Feature 04 `calculated_at` (not on this path; its outages must not stall the screener, T3).
- **Swap (PROPOSED, Phase 1 simplicity).** The single compute thread loads and swaps between screens. Requests queue during the roughly 5–15 s load, twice a day. A separate loader thread is added only if Phase 17 shows the pause matters.

**As-of policy (PROPOSED; decision D3).**
- `as_of` = the newest date in the snapshot's stock rows.
- Each ticker is evaluated at its own last bar on or before `as_of`; call it `at`.
- **Stale** = last bar before `as_of`. **FACT:** 16 tickers today, ADHI since 2026-08-21 (feature04.md §8).
- The default universe excludes stale tickers through a visible, removable chip, "Traded on the as-of date". When stale tickers are included, their rows carry `stale_since`.
- `sessions_ago` counts the ticker's own bars. **FACT:** this is the Feature 04 `ENTITY_SESSIONS` rule and the Backtest's per-ticker bars (CONTRACT §2). The event date is always returned.
- **FACT:** the 2026-09-17/18 gap (M238, OPEN) is missing for every stock, so it is treated exactly as Feature 04 treats it (verify_feature04 F04-06).

**Corporate-action breaks (PROPOSED).**
- **FACT:** D22 (OPEN): PBSA and FORU levels are broken in stored prices.
- A ticker is flagged `CORPORATE_ACTION_BREAK` with the date when it has an `idx_event_annotation` event of a type in `PRICE_ACTION_TYPES` (`datafile.ts:236`) with an ex-date on or after `ADJUSTED_HISTORY_BOUNDARY` (`engine.ts:157`).
- The screener flags; it does not fix. The fix belongs to the data layer (D22).

**Covers:** price, universe, technical. **Does not cover:** flow, which has its own version (T8).

**Risks:**
- A full read evicts part of the 128 MB `shared_buffers`, 2–3 times a day (INFERENCE, low).
- Transfer time is UNKNOWN.

**Verification:**
- Bars from the snapshot equal the published price packs for a sample of tickers: both go through `priceSeries`; read through terminal-api in a test script.
- The version is unchanged across a reload with no data change.
- The version changes when the fixture changes one bar (a case other than the observed one).
- **Permanent.**

## T3. Feature 04 strategy

**Decision (PROPOSED).** Option B without a stored screener layer:
- Feature 04 stays exactly as it is: no column, no VERSION change, no migration, no backfill.
- The screener's default layer is the in-memory memo for each version (T4).
- Feature 04 is the **parity oracle** in automated tests and stays the **AI's** source.
- The screener does not read Feature 04 at runtime.

**Why not read Feature 04 for defaults (rejection with evidence).**
1. **Coverage.** At registry defaults Feature 04 fully serves 9 of 53 indicators (sma 20, macd, rsi 14, bollinger, atr 14, and %B, bandwidth, NATR and stddev derived) and 2 partly (adx without the DIs; the PPO line only). FACT: verify_feature04 F04-17.
2. **Missing inputs.** It stores no open, high, low or volume (FACT), so breakouts, 52-week highs and lows, Supertrend, Stochastic and volume conditions need prices anyway.
3. **Events.** Event conditions need N+1 bars. Multi-day Feature 04 reads across all tickers take 2.2–2.6 s cold, and wide rows sit one per heap page (FACT, feature04.md §9; verify additional findings).
4. **Not materially more efficient.** Computing one default indicator over the full universe from memory takes 80–250 ms once per data version (FACT, benchmark.md §2). The brief's test is "materially more efficient and formula-compatible". Compatibility holds, but efficiency is not material.
5. **Coupling.** The planned 2026-09-17/18 price refill (EXEC F3) would put about 840 equity tickers into `REPAIR_REQUIRED` (FACT from code, verify_feature04 additional findings). A runtime dependency would carry that outage into the screener. A test-only dependency reveals it instead.

**Why not Option A (extend Feature 04).**
- Every indicator would be written twice: TA-Lib and streaming checkpoint state.
- A VERSION bump invalidates all 6,076 checkpoints.
- The engine is copied into stockbit-updater and three more scripts.
- `backfill.py` and `bootstrap_states.py` abort at IHSG.
- The gain for the screener is nothing that compute does not already give.
- FACT: feature04.md §11; verify_feature04 F04-14 and additional findings.

**Why not Option C** (a smaller stored screener snapshot). It adds a store, a refresh job and a second freshness signal for values the memo already holds. INFERENCE.

**Feature 04 roles (PROPOSED).**
- **Parity oracle.** Tests compare `F` on the snapshot with the 15 stored columns and the 4 exact derivations for every equity ticker on `as_of`. Run as a live script on demand and on fixtures in the unit tests.
- **AI consumer:** unchanged.
- **No Feature 04 change now.** Historical semantics are untouched.

**This deviates from the brief's default expectation** ("defaults from precomputed data"). It needs the user's explicit approval: decision D2.

**Class (INFERENCE).** "Stored feature versus shared compute" recurs for every Feature table a UI wants. The rule this sets: store a feature when an independent consumer (the AI, SQL) needs it. Do not store it only to save a sub-second computation that the same TypeScript module already does.

**Verification.**
- Parity test on all equity tickers at the live `as_of`.
- A fixture case where a stored value is deliberately perturbed must make the test fail (another case than the observed one).
- **Permanent.**

---

## T4. Precomputed default path

**PROPOSED source map.**

| Metric family | Source | When computed | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| 53 registry indicators, default and custom | `F` on the snapshot via `Calc` | lazily, for tickers that reach the condition (T7). A **warm set** at each new version = every configuration referenced by the presets (read at runtime from `presets.json`) | `price_version \| key \| canonical params JSON` |
| Last, 1D, ADV20 | snapshot. ADV20 = `liquidity()` (`signals.ts:174-177`, SMA20 of close×volume = the prototype `adv` = the Backtest liquidity) | once per version, all stocks | `price_version` |
| Sector, industry | `IDX_Stock_Universe` only (Universe_Equity_Description is swapped, D23) | once per version | `price_version` |
| Derived transforms (T6) | computed from memo outputs | lazily | `+ transform spec` |
| Flow | T8 | once per broker version | `broker_version` |
| Dividends (Phase 2) | `idx_event_annotation` | once per version | `price_version` |

**One formula path.** Default ("precomputed") and custom ("dynamic") values are the same `F[key](bars, params)` call on the same bars; only the time of the call differs. So they cannot drift apart (INFERENCE from code, `conditions.ts` `Calc.out`).

**What the memo keeps (PROPOSED).**
- For each (configuration, ticker): the last K bars of each output, with K = 261, after computing on the full history. That covers events within N ≤ 120 plus lags, and the 130-bar preview.
- **INFERENCE:** about 1.8 MB per output for the whole universe (845 × 261 × 8 B), so thousands of configurations fit an LRU budget of a few hundred MB.

**Never precomputed or persisted (PROPOSED).**
- Nothing is persisted.
- Raw-level `gt`/`lt` on cumulative outputs (OBV, PVT, A/D, NVI, PVI) is not offered: the level depends on the start bar forever (FACT, verify_matrix_b b-cumulative). These outputs are offered only as states against their own average (with a tie rule), k-bar changes and N-bar highs.
- Long custom lengths are always computed on full history, up to measured caps (T5).

**Result cache (PROPOSED).** A small LRU keyed by (`data_version`, sha256 of the canonical definition) holds response bytes, so repeated preset clicks cost about 0 ms.

**Verification.**
- For each memo configuration, the dynamic value equals a fresh `F` call.
- The memo is invalidated when the version changes.
- **Permanent.**

## T5. One approved indicator contract

**FACT, today's chain.**
- `indRegistry.json`, generated from the workbook, plus `indicators.ts DEFAULTS` go through `build-registry.mjs` to `backtest-registry.json`.
- `backtest-registry.json` is generated and never hand-edited. Its `registry_version` is the content hash of `indRegistry.json` and `indicators.ts`, and `npm run registry:check` fails when it is stale (`apps/backtest-worker/scripts/build-registry.mjs:1-60`).
- The worker exits with `registry_mismatch` on drift (verify_matrix_b additional findings).
- The prototype's `XPARAM` is a hand copy with no min/max, string booleans and 3 `not_accepted` parameters (html_model.md §2.4).

**PROPOSED.**
1. `backtest-registry.json` stays **the** contract for everything it already holds: id, key, name, category, parameter types, defaults, min/max/options, `not_accepted`, inputs, outputs, `price_input`, and formula version (`registry_version`). No screener copy of any of these fields exists anywhere.
2. Screener-only fields go in a **sidecar** keyed by indicator id, `apps/screener-worker/src/core/screen-registry.json`, holding only what the registry does not:
   - `shape` (line, band, dir, osc, pair, adx, vol, cum: the prototype's XK semantics);
   - allowed tests per output (value, state, event);
   - `level_comparable` (false for cumulative outputs);
   - `price_compare_lag` (1 for I10 Donchian, whose bands include the current bar, so `close > upper` can never be true; FACT, matrix_a pattern 7, verify_matrix_a I10);
   - `caps` (a maximum per length parameter, set from Phase 17 measurements by the rule "full-market cold compute at the cap ≤ 2 s on one thread". FACT inputs: CCI at n=1000 takes 7.93 s; SMA, WMA and KAMA at n=1000 take ≤ 0.09 s, verify_matrix_a a-cost-long-length);
   - `warmup_class` (window, recursive, state, cumulative, calendar), for UI hints;
   - `f04` (oracle mapping: params and output → Feature 04 column or exact SQL derivation, with NULLIF on the band width), used **only by tests**.
3. **Why a sidecar now.** Any byte change to `indRegistry.json` or `indicators.ts` changes `registry_version`, and the CLI-deployed worker then refuses to start until it is rebuilt and redeployed (FACT). The sidecar can be merged into `build-registry.mjs` output later, when the Backtest adopts screener semantics (user: Backtest parity is not a priority now).
4. **Versions.**
   - Formulas: `registry_version`.
   - Screener semantics: `screener engine_version`, a content hash over `apps/screener-worker/src/core/**`, the sidecar, `presets.json`, and the backtest core files it imports (the same mechanism as `version.ts`).
5. **Consumers.**
   - `screener-worker` reads the registry and the sidecar at start and refuses to start on any inconsistency.
   - The page reads only `/catalog`, which merges the two, so the frontend holds no definitions.
   - Feature 04 Python (`specs.py`) is unchanged; the oracle mapping lives in the sidecar.
   - AI catalogs are unchanged now.
6. **Drift tests:**
   - every registry id has exactly one sidecar entry and vice versa;
   - every integer length parameter has a cap, and every cap ≥ its default;
   - every output a shape names exists;
   - `warmup_class` is checked on fixture bars by a start-dependence test;
   - `f04` mappings pass on the terminal parity fixtures;
   - the catalog's `registry_version` equals `REGISTRY_VERSION`.

**Class (INFERENCE).** This is the general "derived metadata copied by hand" defect: XPARAM, the I37 label mismatch (reuse.md §7.2), `AI_formula_reference` drift. The rule: one generated artifact plus consumer-specific sidecars whose consistency is a test.

**Permanent;** the sidecar merge is optional later.

## T6. Condition engine

**Wire condition (PROPOSED).** It is the Backtest's `IndicatorCondition` (`conditions.ts:19`) plus only what the screener adds:

```json
{"id":"c2","enabled":true,"kind":"indicator","indicator":"I06","params":{"fast":8},
 "lhs":{"type":"output","output":"macd"},"op":"crosses_above","rhs":{"type":"output","output":"signal"},"within":5}
```

- `kind`: `indicator | price_action | flow | metric`.
- `op`: `gt | lt | between | crosses_above | crosses_below`.
- `rhs`: `{type:'value'} | {type:'range',min,max} | {type:'output'} | {type:'price'}`.
- An optional `derive` on a side (below).
- `within` applies to events only; default 1.

**Semantics (PROPOSED; the class is derived from the operator and the sides).**
- **VALUE** (output against a value or range). `v = side[at]`. `gt`/`lt` are strict. `between` is inclusive, `min ≤ v ≤ max`; the server refuses `min > max` with field `rhs.min` and the message "min must not exceed max". The cell returns value, unit and `date = dates[at]`.
- **STATE** (`gt`/`lt` against an output or the price). `compare(a, op, b)[at]` (`conditions.ts:52-61`). The cell returns lhs, rhs and the date.
- **EVENT** (`crosses_*`, or the switch-on of a state).
  - `s = compare(a, crosses_*, b)`; `j` = the largest index in [at−N+1, at] with `s[j]=1`.
  - The condition passes when such a `j` exists. The cell returns `event_date = dates[j]`, `sessions_ago = at − j`, and the current values.
  - Cross rule (existing): previous ≤ and now >. Bar 0 is never true; NaN is false.
- **Price-action** kinds reuse `PRICE_ACTION`, `priceActionCondition` and `bullishDivergence` (`conditions.ts:124-190`), with a `within` per condition: breakout over the prior N highs, volume spike over the prior N average, SMA cross, MACD divergence.
- **Derived transforms** (new pure module `derive.ts`). Built only from `F` outputs and the exported `sma`, `ema`, `rma`, `wma`, `stdev` (`indicators.ts:46-73`). No indicator formula is added.
  - `pct_from(a,b) = 100·(a/b − 1)`
  - `band_position = 100·(c − lower)/(upper − lower)`, null at zero width
  - `lag(k)`: Donchian prior band; "rising against k bars ago"
  - `rolling_extreme(N, max|min, include_current)`
  - `ma_of(output, SMA|EMA, n)`, with the tie rule "equal is not above"
  - `change(k)`
  - `vs_index(d)`: ticker ROC minus IHSG ROC, aligned with `asOf` (`datafile.ts:259`)
  - `cross_rank`: percentile in the population
  - These cover the prototype's hi52 and lo52 (Donchian 250 + `pct_from`), squeeze (bandwidth + `rolling_extreme`), breakout down (Donchian lower + `lag 1`), rs, rs_rank, silent accumulation (I35 + ROC), "rising" and the cumulative-vs-average states.
  - Only Ichimoku has no registry indicator. It is shown as "requires a new registry indicator" (decision D5).
- **Null handling.**
  - `INDICATOR_OUTPUT_EMPTY` (`conditions.ts:104-107`) is caught per ticker with the `unlessLeftOut` pattern (`signals.ts:261`) and becomes `na:{code:'INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY'}`.
  - A null at `at` becomes `NO_VALUE_AT_DATE`.
  - Flow past the broker data becomes `FLOW_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
  - n/a is "not met", shown with its reason (as the prototype's `na` rule, line 1063).
- **Match and near miss.**
  - `need = entryNeed(logic, at_least, active)` (`conditions.ts:263`, equal to the prototype's `needOf`). `match = met ≥ need`.
  - **Near = !match ∧ active > 1 ∧ need > 1 ∧ met = need − 1.** One rule for the table and the preview. This fixes the prototype's two rules at lines 1180 and 1599 (html_ui.md §3.15).
- **Not reused: `combineEntry`.** It applies one window to every condition, states included (`conditions.ts:269-292`), which is wrong for "today".
- **Ranking and sort inputs.** Each cell carries `sort`: the value for VALUE and STATE, `1000 − sessions_ago` for EVENT (as the prototype). Nulls sort last. Sorting happens in the client (T14).
- **Cross-sectional ranks (PROPOSED, D8).**
  - The population is all stocks with a bar on `as_of`, independent of the user's filters, so a rank does not move when a sector filter changes.
  - It is computed before the per-ticker loop. NaN is excluded from the denominator (fixes prototype defect 9). The population size is returned.

**New pure code (PROPOSED), in `apps/screener-worker/src/core/`:**
- `screen.ts`: evaluate a condition at `at` → cell; a ticker → met, need, status;
- `derive.ts`;
- `definition.ts`: validates a `screen/v1` definition with `BY_ID` and `resolveParams` (`registry.ts:36-73`), sidecar caps and limits;
- `planner.ts` (T7).

**Must not be duplicated:** `F`, `resolveParams`, `compare`, `PRICE_ACTION`, `bullishDivergence`, `flowData`, `brokerNet`, `rollingSum`, `top5Accumulation`, `liquidity`, `entryNeed`, `priceSeries`, `asOf`, `switchOns`.

**Verification:**
- Condition parity: `screen.ts` against `conditionSeries` on the same bars for `gt`, `lt` and the crosses.
- `between` at exactly min and exactly max.

## T7. Query planner

**Stages (PROPOSED).**
0. **Universe.** These filters are conjunctive by definition, outside the match logic (prototype `inUniverse` 1160-1174): stocks only → sector include/exclude → industry → price ≥ → ADV ≥ → traded on `as_of` → universe metric filters. All read snapshot attributes and cost about 0.
1. **Population stage.** Cross-sectional prerequisites (rs_rank) are computed over the fixed population (T6).
2. **Per-ticker loop.** Conditions run in ascending estimated cost:
   - memo hit, snapshot attribute or stored flow: 0;
   - transform of a cached output;
   - dynamic `F` compute, costed by an exponentially weighted average of measured ms per ticker for each indicator key. Derived at runtime, not a hand table.

**Pruning rule (PROPOSED, provably safe).**
- Let n be the number of active conditions and k = need. Let δ = 1 when a near miss is defined (n > 1 and k > 1), else 0.
- After evaluating some conditions with m passes and r remaining, **stop evaluating the ticker iff m + r < k − δ.**
- **Proof:** final met ≤ m + r < k − δ. So met < k (no match), and met ≠ k − 1 when δ = 1 (no near miss). The ticker is neither, and only matches and near misses are displayed.
- **ALL** (k = n): prunes at the second failure, or the first when n = 1.
- **ANY** (k = 1, δ = 0): prunes only after every condition has failed, so there is no saving, and that is correct.
- **AT LEAST k:** prunes once failures exceed n − k + δ.
- A ticker still able to match or be a near miss is evaluated on **all** remaining conditions, because every displayed row needs every cell. Pruning therefore never changes a displayed value or count.
- Order affects cost only, never results.
- Because the memo is kept per ticker, a pruned ticker is never computed. "Calculate only what is necessary" holds per (ticker, configuration).

**Cancellation.** A cancel flag is checked between tickers (edge-bff "latest wins").

**Verification:**
- A property test: random definitions on the fixture universe give the same match set, near set and displayed cells with pruning on and off, over many seeds.
- A test for each logic mode, plus n = 1.
- **Permanent.**

biggest_risks: Deviation from the brief's expected 'defaults from Feature 04' path: the design computes defaults in memory and uses Feature 04 only as a test oracle. If the user rejects this, T3/T4 change (D2).

Mixed split adjustment in stored prices (ERRORS D22, PBSA, FORU) makes every price-based screen list affected tickers as oversold or far below their averages. The screener can only flag them; the fix belongs to the data layer and needs a go.

UNKNOWN in-region time and memory to stream 1.33M price rows and a 61-session Feature 05 window into Node. If either is slow, the 5-15 s version swap pause or cold start may need a loader thread or an incremental tail update (Phase 17 decides).
One full price read per version on a cache-starved database (shared_buffers 128 MB, AI workload shares it). The impact is expected small (2-3 reads a day) but is unmeasured.

Planned price refill EXEC F3 would put about 840 Feature 04 tickers into REPAIR_REQUIRED. The screener does not depend on Feature 04 at runtime, but the parity tests will fail until Feature 04 is repaired; the refill must be sequenced.
Broker data lags price whenever no new Stockbit token is supplied (M243, verify_flow C2). Flow conditions are then evaluated on an older date; users may misread them despite the label.
Version skew between edge-bff (page) and screener-worker deployments, and M252 merge-commit deploy skips. Mitigated by GitHub deploy for both plus versions in every response, but not eliminated.

Prototype UX changes users will notice: legacy technical entries replaced by registry indicators and transforms, unavailable filters disabled, convention differences (RVOL, KVO, OBV start, PSAR) because F is authoritative.
Single compute thread serializes screens. Under concurrency, queueing could exceed the deadline. Thread count and queue depth must come from Phase 17.

Send to Backtest touches the same Backtest boot() as the BACKTEST-LOAD plan (another session's code; M248 overwrite history). The per-condition 'within' semantics are lossy against the Backtest's single window.
